issues.summary: Bearer token sent to pre-signed Canvas upload URL, conflating owned-endpoint auth with delegated-URL auth
evidence: _upload_file_to_canvas (main.py:198) calls make_canvas_request for the pre-signed upload_url, which always injects 'Authorization: Bearer {api_key}' (utils.py:53)

Pre-signed URLs carry their own auth credentials in the URL parameters; sending an additional Bearer token is unexpected and may interfere with some Canvas storage backends that reject unrecognized auth headers on pre-signed requests
issues.suggestion: For the pre-signed URL upload step, bypass make_canvas_request and call requests.request directly (or use a separate helper that omits the Authorization header). Add a comment explaining that pre-signed URLs are self-authenticating. This makes the trust boundary explicit: owned Canvas endpoints use Bearer auth; delegated upload URLs use the embedded signature.

root_causes: The Canvas integration was authored with make_canvas_request as the only HTTP dispatch function, without distinguishing between Canvas-owned endpoints (needing Bearer auth) and pre-signed delegated URLs (self-authenticating). The abstraction does not model the two different trust contexts.
